clue.text: Vessel used in a service in church

indicators.note: in means the service and the A are placed inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
the RAF (Royal Air Force) is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Some sacred vessel is being put to use during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is a glass container for serving wine or water, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: State of officer having trouble containing soldiers

indicators.note: containing means the officer and trouble words hold the soldiers between them

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel
ado means fuss or trouble
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: An officer is having bother keeping his troops in check.
explanation.definitionFit: Colorado is one of the states of the USA.

clue.text: Second-rate newspaper's charity event

definitions.meaning: a scurrilous low-quality paper is disparagingly called this
students' fund-raising week of stunts for charity, as at British universities

explanation.surface: A tabloid is running a charity event.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a student rag is an annual charity fund-raising event.
explanation.definitionFit: Rag means both a shoddy newspaper and a student charity event.

clue.text: Inane sports administrators acceptable in all of France

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, which runs English football

indicators.note: in means the acceptable letter goes inside the French word for all

parts.note: tous is French for all
U means upper-class, hence socially acceptable

explanation.surface: Foolish sports officials are welcome everywhere in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatuous means silly and pointless, just as inane does.

clue.text: Breaking legs so badly is jolly stupid!

indicators.note: breaking means the marine splits the reshuffled letters apart by sitting inside them
badly signals that the letters of legs so are put in a wrong order

parts.note: a jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that it is very foolish to break your legs so badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like 'very' qualifying 'stupid', but it is old naval slang for a Royal Marine; the marine sits inside the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gormless is a British colloquial word for dim-witted or lacking sense.

clue.text: At home more, keeping girl without food? It's bizarre!

definitions.note: the definition names the quality of being bizarre, a noun

indicators.note: keeping means the stay-at-home phrase holds the girl-and-food piece within it

parts.note: someone who is at home more goes out less, so the phrase is read as out less

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the girl's name wraps round the food word

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
a dish is a serving of food

explanation.surface: Someone who stays in, keeping a girl hungry, is behaving strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At home more' is a cryptic phrase: stay in more and you go out less. 'without' means outside, as in old usage, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlandishness is strangeness, the state of something being weird or odd.

clue.text: Wine forced on Gershwin

indicators.note: on means the forced word comes first, sitting above the name in the down light

parts.note: made means compelled or forced
Ira Gershwin was the lyricist brother of George

explanation.surface: Someone forced wine on a Gershwin.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a fortified wine from the Portuguese island of that name.

clue.text: Without reserve, divorcee finally set dog on man

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse, a divorcee

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of set is used

parts.note: Rover is a stock name for a dog
Ted is a man's name

explanation.surface: A divorcee at last sets her dog on a man.
explanation.definitionFit: An extroverted person is outgoing, so lacking reserve.

clue.text: Something that wears down an engineer?

definitions.meaning: a thing that saps, exhausting strength gradually
a private in the Royal Engineers is called this

explanation.walkthrough: In the British army a sapper is a soldier of the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapper names both a thing that drains energy and a military engineer.

clue.text: Like silence, hard to obtain in rustic bird

parts.note: the proverb says silence is golden

indicators.note: obtain in means the hard letter is got inside the countryman word

parts.note: a peasant is a rustic country person
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A country bird is as quiet as silence and hard to come by.
explanation.definitionFit: The golden pheasant is a brightly coloured game bird from China.

clue.text: Settled by window, as burglars try to be?

indicators.note: by means the word for settled is placed next to the word for window

parts.note: a light is a pane or window
to foot a bill is to settle it, so footed means settled

explanation.surface: A house that has been sold sits beside a window, while burglars try to tread softly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settled' is the past tense of footing a bill, not of coming to rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Burglars want to move quietly and nimbly, being agile and soft of tread.

clue.text: Replace striking-head of pile-driver?

definitions.meaning: read as re-place, to put back: the word for put written back to front
the heavy head of a pile-driver, also the ram, is called this

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: 'Replace' read as put back gives the word for put reversed. The second is a technical term for the part of a pile-driver that strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: The rammer of a pile-driver is its tup, and a tup is also a male sheep that butts.

clue.text: Come back about son's provision for 15

parts.note: re means about or concerning
S is the abbreviation for son
15-across is ducks and drakes, and a pond is what ducks and drakes are provided with

explanation.surface: Someone is replying about their son's arrangements for a fifteen.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 15 points to the birds of 15-across, for whom a pond is laid on.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond is to reply, to come back with an answer.

clue.text: Attempt to anticipate additional visitors taking time out

parts.note: a second helping is an additional one

indicators.note: out means the time letter is removed from the visitors word

parts.note: guests are visitors

explanation.surface: Someone tries to foresee more visitors arriving after time out.
explanation.definitionFit: To second-guess is to predict what someone will do, anticipating them.

clue.text: Fatty's quiet farewell to Spanish and English gathered round

indicators.note: gathered round means the Spanish goodbye encloses the quiet letter

parts.note: adios is goodbye to a Spanish speaker
P (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: A fat man quietly bids goodbye to the Spanish and the English as they gather round.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose describes fatty tissue, so the adjective means fatty.

clue.text: Game birds?

parts.note: read not as birds shot for sport but as male and female waterfowl that are the name of a game

explanation.definitionFit: The pastime of skimming flat stones over water is named after male and female waterfowl.

clue.text: They say yours truly cries out for frozen food

indicators.note: they say signals that the words are spoken and heard as the answer

parts.note: yours truly means I, the speaker, and cries out means screams, giving I scream

explanation.surface: Someone shrieks for frozen food, so people report.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice cream is a frozen dessert, a frozen food.

clue.text: Not keen to alter nice sunsuit and hat

indicators.note: to alter means these letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is reluctant to change a pleasant sunsuit and hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to alter' rearranges NICE SUNSUIT and HAT; 'and' just joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unenthusiastic means lacking eagerness, the same as not keen.

clue.text: Final directions about this country's carved ornaments

parts.note: a net figure is the final one after deductions

indicators.note: about means the compass points go round the country

parts.note: S and E are compass directions
UK is this country to a British newspaper

explanation.surface: Final instructions concern the carved ornaments of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Netsuke are small Japanese carved toggles, decorative ornaments.

clue.text: Benbow, say, like Crichton lacking breadth and energy

indicators.note: lacking means the letters for breadth and energy are taken away

parts.note: The Admirable Crichton is J M Barrie's play about a butler
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Benbow is compared with Crichton but lacks breadth and energy.
explanation.walkthrough: John Benbow was a famous English admiral; J M Barrie's play is The Admirable Crichton.
explanation.definitionFit: Benbow was a naval commander, an example of a flag officer, so 'say' marks an example.

clue.text: Lorry touring cold area up north

indicators.note: touring means the lorry goes round the cold letter

parts.note: artic is British slang for an articulated lorry

explanation.surface: A lorry tours a cold region in the far north.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic is the polar region at the top of the globe.

clue.text: Inspector Wexford attending army race meeting?

parts.note: Reg Wexford is Ruth Rendell's fictional detective inspector
at means present at, attending
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A fictional detective goes to an army race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth Rendell's Chief Inspector Wexford has the first name Reg.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a series of boat races, a meeting for racing on water; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: Wandering distortion of coda in Mahler's First

indicators.note: distortion of means the letters are twisted into a different order
first means only the opening letter of Mahler is taken

explanation.surface: A coda in a Mahler First Symphony has been distorted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distortion of' rearranges CODA IN together with M, the first letter of Mahler.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic people roam from place to place, so the word means wandering.

clue.text: Film backed by European supporter on course

indicators.note: backed means the film title is written back to front

parts.note: ET is Spielberg's film about an extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: A film is financed by a European fan at a racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' looks like 'financed' but reverses ET; the 'course' is a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course a tee is the peg that supports the ball before driving.

clue.text: Retiring union leader ingenuous about replacing of lock

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word union
about means the word for ingenuous wraps round the other piece

parts.note: naive means innocent or ingenuous

indicators.note: replacing of means the letters of the hair word are rearranged

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A retiring trade union leader is too naive about changing a lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' suggests a door fitting but is a tress of hair; the anagram is of that synonym, not of a printed word.
explanation.definitionFit: A retiring person is shy and reserved, which is to say unassertive.

clue.text: Indisposed to exclude British from draft law

indicators.note: to exclude means the British letter is removed

parts.note: a bill is a proposed law

explanation.surface: Someone is unwilling to keep Britain out of a proposed law.
explanation.definitionFit: Indisposed means slightly unwell, which is ill.

clue.text: It may contain film of Nutcracker, eliminating noise

indicators.note: eliminating means the noise word is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: Casse-Noisette is the French title of Tchaikovsky's Nutcracker ballet
the word noise is taken as written

explanation.surface: A film of the Nutcracker ballet is put out without the noise.
explanation.walkthrough: Tchaikovsky's ballet is known in French as Casse-Noisette; 'eliminating' takes NOISE out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassette is a case of magnetic tape, and video cassettes hold film.

clue.text: During attack, see obstacle race

indicators.note: during means the look word sits inside the attack word

parts.note: to slam is to attack or criticise fiercely
lo is an old word meaning see or look

explanation.surface: In the middle of an assault, someone watches an obstacle race.
explanation.definitionFit: A slalom is a race weaving between obstacles such as gates or poles.
